children: Addus HomeCare agreed to acquire AccentCare's personal care division for an anticipated purchase price of about $275 million.

The home care services provider said Monday the deal would expand its personal care service capabilities in key markets like Texas, Illinois, California and Arizona, while adding operations in six additional states including Colorado, Georgia, Minnesota, Pennsylvania, Tennessee and Washington.
The transaction includes AccentCare's personal care operations outside of New York, and does not relate to its hospice and home health operations, the companies said.
Addus said it expects the deal to add about $280 million in annualized personal care revenue, representing a roughly 19% increase to its revenue base.

"This acquisition continues our growth strategy to leverage our strong personal care experience to build scale in existing markets as well as enter select new markets," Addus's Chief Executive Dirk Allison said.
The company expects to close the transaction following completion of regulatory approvals and subject to customary closing conditions.
Addus plans to fund the acquisition through a combination of its revolving credit facility and cash on hand.
